executive_summary: The shop's resilience is compromised by a few critical weaknesses. Latency on core services (product-catalog, frontend, astronomy-db) instantly degrades all user journeys, indicating a wide blast radius. Hidden dependencies - astronomy-db affecting checkout and flagd affecting cart - are not captured in the current dependency map, exposing unexpected failure paths. Additionally, valkey-cart and cart themselves act as single points of failure, each causing full cart-journey loss when they crash. weaknesses.title: Wide blast radius from latency on core services
weaknesses.explanation: Injecting 300ms latency on product-catalog, frontend or astronomy-db aborts the experiment and triggers watchdog breaches, causing all four key journeys (cart, checkout, home, product) to degrade. The impact is 1.00 with full breadth, showing a single latency fault can cascade across the entire shop.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-164224-dcfe (product-catalog) impact 1.00 breadth 1.00; exp-141542-f9bb (frontend) impact 1.00 breadth 1.00; exp-143142-3011 (astronomy-db) impact 1.00 breadth 1.00; all aborted due to p95 >800ms

fix.fix_title: Add circuit breaker, retries and replica scaling
fix.steps: Introduce a client-side circuit breaker (e.g., resilience4j) around calls from frontend to product-catalog and astronomy-db with a 500 ms timeout and 3 retries. Deploy each core service with 2 replicas and set restart: unless-stopped so containers auto-recover on crash.
fix.compose_override:
services:
  product-catalog:
    restart: unless-stopped
  astronomy-db:
    restart: unless-stopped
  frontend:
    restart: unless-stopped
fix.expected_effect: Latency faults no longer cascade; p95 stays below 800 ms and journeys complete even when one instance is delayed.

weaknesses.title: Hidden dependency on checkout via astronomy-db
weaknesses.explanation: Delays on astronomy-db cause checkout journey latency breaches even though the dependency map did not predict checkout involvement. This hidden coupling expands failure impact beyond expected paths.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-143142-3011 delay 300ms on astronomy-db degraded checkout (p95 1244ms >800ms); verdict PARTIAL; note "HIDDEN dependency on checkout"

fix.fix_title: Add retry, timeout and circuit breaker for checkout-astronomy-db calls
fix.steps: Wrap checkout service HTTP client calls to astronomy-db with a 400 ms timeout, 2 retries and a circuit breaker that opens after 5 consecutive failures. On open, return cached product data or a graceful error message. Log each fallback event.
fix.expected_effect: Checkout journey remains within SLA despite 300 ms delays in astronomy-db, eliminating hidden coupling impact.

weaknesses.title: Hidden dependency on cart via flagd
weaknesses.explanation: A crash of flagd aborts the experiment and degrades the cart journey, despite no predicted journeys. This reveals an undocumented reliance of cart on flagd, a risk for unanticipated outages.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-141616-6842 crash on flagd degraded cart (p95 3051ms >800ms); verdict REFUTED; note "HIDDEN dependency on cart"

fix.fix_title: Circuit breaker and fallback for flagd in cart
fix.steps: Instrument cart service flag-evaluation with a circuit breaker (200 ms timeout, 1 retry). When the breaker opens, use locally stored default flags. Deploy a second flagd replica and add restart: unless-stopped to ensure availability.
fix.expected_effect: Cart journey no longer fails when flagd crashes; fallback flags keep cart functional.

weaknesses.title: Single point of failure in valkey-cart
weaknesses.explanation: Crashing valkey-cart aborts the experiment and fully impacts the cart journey, with a breadth of 0.25. The service is a sole source for cart state, making its failure a critical SPOF.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-104221-fd4f crash on valkey-cart impact 1.00 breadth 0.25; degraded cart; verdict PARTIAL

fix.steps: Run two valkey-cart containers behind DNS round-robin. Configure the cart client to use Redis Sentinel-style failover with a 300 ms reconnect timeout. Add restart: unless-stopped to both instances to auto-recover.
fix.expected_effect: Valkey-cart crash no longer aborts experiments; cart state remains available via failover.

weaknesses.title: Single point of failure in cart service
weaknesses.explanation: A crash of the cart service aborts the experiment and fully degrades the cart journey, confirming cart as a SPOF for its own functionality and for downstream checkout.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-142250-d200 crash on cart impact 1.00 breadth 0.25; degraded cart; verdict PARTIAL

fix.fix_title: Scale cart service and add retry logic
fix.steps: Deploy two cart service replicas behind the existing load balancer. Add restart: unless-stopped. In internal cart calls, add a 2-retry policy with a 250 ms timeout to handle transient failures.
fix.expected_effect: Cart service is no longer a single point of failure; crashes are absorbed by the replica and retries keep journeys alive.

formula: penalty = 100 x (0.5 x impact + 0.3 x breadth + 0.2 x recovery); service score = 100 - worst penalty on that service; overall = mean of service scores weighted by the number of journeys the service sits on (at least 1; the larger of the map's count and the journeys it was seen to degrade).
methodology: An independent synthetic prober exercises four user journeys (home, product, cart, checkout) through the front proxy every second. It is the ground truth and does not depend on the application's own telemetry.

A baseline run fixes per-journey error rate and p95 latency and derives safety thresholds from them. A watchdog aborts any experiment that breaches a threshold or loses sight of the prober. An advisory safety agent re-checks the live measurements every few seconds and may abort earlier; it can never cancel a watchdog abort, extend a fault or change a threshold.

Each experiment injects one fault (container crash, added network delay or packet loss), measures every journey during the fault window (up to the abort for aborted runs), reverts the fault, and measures how long the journeys take to return inside the baseline band.

Impact, breadth, recovery and the penalty are computed deterministically from those measurements. The hypothesis verdict compares the journeys the planner predicted would degrade with those that actually did: CONFIRMED when equal, PARTIAL when they overlap, REFUTED when they do not.
A hidden dependency is a journey that degraded by at least 0.3 although neither the hypothesis nor the dependency map expected it.

The analyst agent ranks weaknesses and the fixer agent proposes fixes from the measured results only; their output is validated against known experiments, services and an allowlist of compose keys. When Groq is unavailable or its output is invalid, rule-based fallbacks produce the same sections. Fixes are proposals and are never applied.
